Language Model and ApplicationA large language model (LLM) generates text from the context supplied to a call

The interface, model and surrounding application have different responsibilities

ChatGPT and Language ModelsHistorical 2025 example

A chat interface accepts instructions and generates text

Historical LLM ComparisonOriginal benchmark snapshot, not a current universal ranking of language models

The original benchmark compares models under its own evaluation conditions

A Single LLM Call

One model call maps its supplied input to an output

Limits of a Single Call

External context, tools and multi-step work need an application around the model

LLM Application Control Flow

Applications place retrieval, tool calls and other steps around model calls

Chains of Calls

A chain connects the inputs and outputs of multiple application steps

LangChain

Reusable components can be composed into larger LLM applications

LangChain Components

Models, prompts, memory, indexes, chains and tools play different roles

LangChain, LangGraph and LangSmithThe ecosystem separates application components, execution control and observation

Components construct the calls, while traces help diagnose what happened

An Email Transformation PromptThe source complaint and requested tone become one concrete prompt

An instruction and customer email specify a concrete transformation task

The Transformed EmailCompare the rewritten tone with the facts in the original blender complaint

The model response can be compared with the requested style and source message

Prompt TemplatesHistorical 2025 example

A template names the variable fields within a reusable instruction

Why Prompt Templates?Historical 2025 example

Reusable templates separate common instructions from changing task inputs

Structured Output and ValidationA parser turns generated text into fields the application can check

Parseable JSON can still contain an unsupported value

Parsing the Returned OutputParsing the JSON and checking field types are separate steps

The returned JSON is parsed into fields that the application can inspect

Conversation History as InputThe application supplies selected earlier turns as context for a later call

A stateless call needs relevant conversation history supplied in its input

A Follow-Up QuestionHistorical 2025 example

A later question can depend on information from an earlier turn

A Simple Sequential ChainHistorical 2025 example

The output of the first call becomes input to the next call

Inspecting Sequential OutputThe first call names the company and the second describes that generated company

Intermediate and final outputs show what the connected calls actually produced

A Chain with Several Inputs

Named values can flow through several branches and later calls

A Router Chain

A routing decision selects a destination chain for the input

Router Chain ExecutionThe router selects physics before the destination answers the radiation question

The observed route and returned answer connect the decision with execution

Retrieval and GenerationRAG retrieves external text and includes it in the input used to generate an answer

Retrieval changes the information supplied to a call without retraining the model

Context Window and Token BudgetContext limits depend on the model and count tokens rather than a universal word limit

4 x 1,200 = 4,800 fits the 5,000-token evidence budget

Why Retrieve Context?Historical illustration: the quoted word limit is not a universal limit for current models

Current limits depend on the model and token budget, including the reserved answer

The RAG Pipeline

Loading, splitting, storage, retrieval and generation form one connected pipeline

Text Embeddings

An embedding maps text into a vector representation

Embedding Similarity

Related sentences can have nearby representations despite different wording

Vectors and Original Chunks

The index stores vector representations alongside their original text

Search with a Question Vector

The question representation selects nearby document representations

Generation from Retrieved Text

Retrieved text becomes context in the model input

The Catalog Question and AnswerThe catalog answer needs supporting product records and a check for missing matches

The question, returned products and answer belong to the same catalog task

Vector Database SearchThe shirt query searches vectors and returns document records, rather than a final answer

The question vector retrieves candidate documents from the index

Passing Retrieved Context to the ModelRetrieved page_content is joined into qdocs and supplied with the catalog question

The prompt connects the retrieved source text with the user question

StuffStuff sends selected passages together in one context, within its token budget

Stuffing supplies the selected documents together in one model context

Map ReduceMap calls process passages independently, then a reduce call combines their outputs

Per-document outputs can be combined into a later reduction step

RefineRefine revises a running answer, so document order can affect its result

Each document can revise an answer created from earlier documents

Map RerankMap rerank selects a scored candidate, and its score is not a correctness probability

Candidate answers can be scored and a selected answer returned

Indexing and Answering Paths

Document preparation and per-question retrieval run at different times

Document Source Types

Structured and unstructured sources can be loaded through different integrations

Document Splitting

A boundary can separate the pieces needed to answer one question

Chunk Size and OverlapWith length_function=len, chunk_size and chunk_overlap are character counts

Chunk length and shared boundaries determine which text stays together

Caveat: Broken ConditionsA cut can separate an instruction from its condition

The stop instruction loses its threshold after a bad cut

Retrieval Strategies

Similarity, diversity, metadata and model assistance address different retrieval needs

Maximal Marginal Relevance

Retrieval can balance similarity to the question with diversity among results

The MMR Selection Steps

A larger candidate pool is narrowed to a relevant and diverse subset

Model-Assisted Retrieval

A model can turn a user question into a more useful search query

Contextual Compression

A compression step keeps relevant parts of retrieved content

A Similarity Search ExampleThe mushroom example compares similar candidates with a more diverse selected set

The returned documents expose what the embedding search actually selected

Caveat: Similar but WrongSimilar wording can belong to an obsolete rule

Both P-17 versions mention the same pressure question

Similarity and EligibilityA higher similarity score cannot make a withdrawn document eligible

The eligible manual can rank below an ineligible one in this two-dimensional example

Question Answering from Retrieved Text

Relevant documents are assembled into context for answer generation

The Retrieval QA FlowThe question retrieves documents whose text enters the answering prompt

A question selects documents whose text supports the model answer

Checking the EvidenceDoes the selected text answer this question for this equipment?

Current P-17 pressure text supports the requested value

Checking the AnswerDoes the cited text support the value and unit in the answer?

The citation must support the claim beside it

Locating an Answer FailureEvaluate retrieval and answer support separately on the same question set

StageIllustrative resultRemaining failure
Evidence found10 / 12 questions2 retrieval misses
Supported answer given evidence8 / 102 unsupported answers
End-to-end supported answer8 / 124 failed questions
Improving generation alone cannot recover the two missing-evidence cases

Conversational Retrieval

Conversation history can affect the question used for retrieval

RAG Evaluation BoundariesSaved intermediate artifacts separate retrieval failures from answer failures

End-to-end correctness is 6/10, while correctness with evidence present is 6/8

Takeaway: LLM Systems

1Prompts, parsers and selected history define the input and output of each model call
2Chains pass named values between steps, while routing chooses a destination
3RAG prepares source documents, selects eligible evidence and checks the resulting answer
